speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a child with a fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics, I need to know what specific antibiotic you were prescribed and when you started taking it. 

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Complete_Blood_Count, Antinuclear_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your blood work is normal, I need to ask: Did you develop the rash immediately after receiving the antibiotic injection, or did it appear hours later? Also, do you have any swollen lymph nodes?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy, Serum_IgE

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your skin biopsy and IgE levels are normal, I need to know: What specific antibiotic did you take, and did the rash appear after a dose of penicillin or cephalosporin? Also, has anyone else in your family had a similar reaction to antibiotics?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) syndrome secondary to amoxicillin.

REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide a dermatology image of the rash distribution in the antecubital and popliteal fossae for confirmation.
